verses.text: After this the Moabites, Ammonites, and some of the Meunites came to make war on Jehoshaphat.
Messengers told him, "A huge army is coming against you from Syria, from beyond the sea. They're already at Hazazon Tamar," that is, En Gedi.
Jehoshaphat was alarmed, so he turned to the LORD for help and called for a fast throughout Judah.
People gathered from every town in Judah to ask the LORD for help.
Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard in the LORD's house, among the people gathered from Judah and Jerusalem.
He said, "LORD, God of our ancestors, aren't you the God in heaven who rules over every kingdom on earth? Power and might are in your hands. No one can stand against you.
Didn't you drive out the people of this land before your people Israel and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham, your friend?
They settled here and built a sanctuary to honor your name. They said,

'If disaster comes on us, whether war, judgment, disease, or famine, we'll stand before this house and before you, because your name is here. We'll cry out to you in our trouble, and you'll hear us and save us.'
Now look at the people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir. When Israel came out of Egypt, you kept them from invading those lands. Israel went around them and left them alive.
Look how they're repaying us. They've come to drive us out of the land you gave us as our inheritance.
Our God, won't you judge them? We're powerless against this huge army coming at us. We don't know what to do, but our eyes are on you."
All Judah stood before the LORD, with their wives, children, and little ones.
Then the LORD's Spirit came on Jahaziel as he stood in the assembly. He was a Levite from Asaph's family, the son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah.
He said, "Listen, everyone in Judah and Jerusalem, and you too, King Jehoshaphat. The LORD says, 'Don't let this huge army frighten or discourage you. The battle belongs to God.
Tomorrow go down to meet them. They'll be coming up the Pass of Ziz, and you'll find them at the end of the valley in front of the wilderness of Jeruel.

You won't have to fight this battle. Take your positions, stand your ground, and see how the LORD rescues you, Judah and Jerusalem. Don't be afraid or lose heart. Go out to meet them tomorrow. The LORD is with you.'"
Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground, and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem bowed before the LORD and worshiped him.
The Levites from the families of Kohath and Korah stood up and praised the LORD, the God of Israel, with loud voices.

Early the next morning they went out into the wilderness of Tekoa. As they set out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, Judah and Jerusalem! Trust the LORD your God and you'll stand firm. Trust his prophets and you'll succeed."

After talking it over with the people, he appointed singers to go in front of the army in sacred clothing, praising the LORD with these words: "Give thanks to the LORD, for his faithful love lasts forever."
As they began singing and praising, the LORD set ambushes against the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who had marched against Judah. They were struck down.
The Ammonites and Moabites turned on the people of Mount Seir and wiped them out. Once they had finished with Seir, they turned on one another.
When Judah reached the lookout over the wilderness, they saw bodies lying on the ground where the huge army had been. No one had escaped.

Jehoshaphat and his people went to collect the plunder. They found valuables everywhere and stripped precious jewels from the dead, more than they could carry. There was so much that it took three days to gather it.
On the fourth day they gathered in the Valley of Beracah and blessed the LORD there. That's why the place is still called the Valley of Beracah.
Then everyone from Judah and Jerusalem returned to Jerusalem with Jehoshaphat leading them. They were joyful because the LORD had given them cause to celebrate over their enemies.
They entered Jerusalem with stringed instruments, harps, and trumpets and went to the LORD's house.
Fear of God came over all the surrounding kingdoms when they heard the LORD had fought against Israel's enemies.
Jehoshaphat's kingdom was at peace because his God gave him rest on every side.
Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king of Judah. He ruled for twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
He followed the way of his father Asa and kept to it, doing what was right in the LORD's eyes.
The high places remained, though, and the people still hadn't set their hearts on the God of their ancestors.
The rest of what Jehoshaphat did, from first to last, is recorded in the history of Jehu son of Hanani, included in the Book of the Kings of Israel.
After this, King Jehoshaphat of Judah made an alliance with King Ahaziah of Israel, who acted very wickedly.
They joined together to build ships for Tarshish, building them at Ezion Geber.

Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat: "Because you joined forces with Ahaziah, the LORD has destroyed what you built." The ships were wrecked and couldn't sail to Tarshish.
